name: Supabase
tagline: A backend platform to evaluate for database, authentication, storage and application data workflows.
description: Supabase is a backend platform to evaluate for applications that need database-backed services and related developer workflows. Fit depends on data access rules, deployment model, backup and recovery, usage, integrations and operational ownership; verify current limits and terms.
pros: A small proof of concept can test database and application integration together.
Access policies and data model can be validated with realistic user roles.
Backup, export and migration can be tested before production adoption.
cons: Database security depends on correctly designed and tested access policies.
Usage, storage, compute and egress may affect cost as the application grows.
A managed backend still requires backup, monitoring and incident ownership.

content.title: Model the data and access
content.body: Build a small schema that represents the core application records. Test each operation as an anonymous user, authenticated user and administrator. Confirm that one user cannot read or change another user's records and that service credentials are never exposed to the client.

content.title: Deployment and operations
content.body: Determine who owns schema migrations, environment separation, secrets, backups and incident response. Test a migration in staging, restore a backup and document the rollback path. Verify the service's supported regions and deployment options against requirements.

content.title: Performance and usage
content.body: Run a representative read/write workload and record latency, query patterns, storage, connections and data growth. Check current usage quotas and overage behavior. Do not assume that a successful small demo predicts peak production behavior.

content.title: Integrations and portability
content.body: Test authentication, storage and any external services the app needs. Export a sample database and files, then verify that the export is usable. Document which platform-specific functions would need replacement if the app moved to another backend.

content.title: Security and cost
content.body: Review access policies, logging, retention, backup frequency, admin roles and key rotation. Model database, storage, bandwidth, compute and support using expected and peak usage, then confirm current plan limits directly.

faqs.question: Who should evaluate Supabase?
faqs.answer: Evaluate Supabase when its primary workflow matches a documented requirement. Run a representative pilot and verify current capabilities, limits and contract terms directly with the vendor.

faqs.question: Are prices and ratings independently verified here?
faqs.answer: No. This review does not present an independently verified price or third-party rating. Check current official documentation and obtain a dated quote.

faqs.question: What should a pilot include?
faqs.answer: Test the main workflow, one failure case, permissions, integrations, export and offboarding. Record pass, partial pass, fail or unknown and assign an owner to every unresolved requirement.

faqs.question: How should total cost be compared?
faqs.answer: Include licenses, usage, implementation, migration, training, integrations, support, internal administration and renewal terms—not only the headline subscription.

author: Marcus Rivera
learningCurve: Minimal — most users can get started within an hour
whoShouldUse: Supabase is ideal for small to mid-size teams that need a reliable developer tools solution without excessive complexity. It works well for organizations with 5-200 users who prioritize ease of use and quick deployment.
whoShouldNotUse: Supabase may not be suitable for large enterprises with complex compliance requirements or teams needing extensive customization options. Organizations with more than 500 users may find the pricing less competitive at scale.
